summary: Cross-account burst charge from orphaned AWS integration appearing on finalized invoice
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (BlueHarbor Analytics) reports a one-off burst charge on their finalized invoice (INV-2026-03-08-BH-0042). Charge labeled as 'burst credits' for a 15-minute window on 2026-03-08 02:11–02:26 UTC. Customer asserts they did not initiate production traffic during that window and that their dedicated pool should have covered traffic.

Impact:
- Unexpected $1,120 line item on finalized invoice for a mid-sized enterprise customer (billing dispute).
- Customer concerned about cross-account attribution and possible leaked access from an old AWS integration.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment in us-west (BlueHarbor: dedicated cluster dh-west-03).
- Invoice finalized; autopay withheld pending dispute.

Steps to reproduce / observed timeline:
1) 2026-03-08 02:10 UTC: scheduled KV-cache warmup job (staging) should run for internal testing only — customer claims it was cancelled.
2) 2026-03-08 02:11–02:26 UTC: sudden spike in requests attributed to key bh-prod-01 (production API key).
3) Billing pipeline classified those tokens as burst credits due to crossing preserved-reserve thresholds.
4) Postback reconciler processed postbacks from multiple proxies; some postbacks carried an aws-integration identifier `aws-int-77-orphaned`.

Logs / attachments:
- Invoice screenshot and CSV attached by customer (attached_files/invoice_INV-2026-03-08-BH-0042.csv).
- Sample server logs for bh-prod-01 (support artifacts).

Initial customer request:
Please investigate how a staging/cancelled job could be billed against production, and whether an orphaned AWS integration forwarded or re-wrote the API key attribution. Customer requests provisional credit and root cause so they can clear autopay.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Aisha Patel: Acknowledged receipt. I've opened an internal trace request with Billing and Cloud-Integrations. Will post ETA for first-pass triage by EOD.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Marco Gomez: Pulling logs from postback-reconciler for 2026-03-08 02:00–03:00 UTC. Noting repeated proxy hop via edge-proxy-9 with header X-Forwarded-For chain containing an AWS lambda ID. Attaching correlating trace IDs.

2026-03-10 13:40 - BlueHarbor (contact: Elena Cho): Confirmed they cancelled the KV warmup at 01:58 UTC and that no other scheduled batch should have targeted bh-prod-01. They've provided the cancellation timestamp and an internal job-id (bh-j-993).

2026-03-11 08:30 - Billing (J. Nguyen): Preliminary reconciliation shows 2,800 burst tokens billed under bh-prod-01 during the window. Postback paths show origin tag "aws-int-77-orphaned" which maps to an old AWS connector previously decommissioned for another tenant (INT-614).

2026-03-12 10:05 - Marco Gomez: Root cause hypothesis: orphaned AWS integration (aws-int-77) was still programmed into a third-party proxy that rewrote the API key header during a deploy on 2026-03-08. That proxy belonged to a partner account that had a stale mapping to bh-prod-01 due to an earlier org-merge. Engineering is validating whether the proxy rewrite created a cross-account attribution loop.
2026-03-13 14:12 - Aisha Patel: Customer notified of provisional credit and next steps. They accepted the temporary credit pending final reconciliation.
2026-03-13 15:30 - BlueHarbor (Elena Cho): Thanks — provisional credit applied is sufficient for now. Please share final RCA and remediation steps.
2026-03-13 16:00 - Marco Gomez: Marking ticket resolved after final audit and credit. Follow-up task created for Cloud Integrations to remove orphaned mapping and add a post-deploy check (INT-722).
investigation_notes: Checked postback-reconciler traces for proxy headers and forward chain; found repeated header rewrite pattern: 'x-rw-api-key: bh-prod-01' introduced by edge-proxy-9 with tag aws-int-77-orphaned.

Cross-referenced aws-int-77 against internal inventory: previously belonged to partner account 'StreamSet Partners' and was decommissioned 2025-12-12 but the proxy config in partner infra was not purged (deployment drift).

Billing aggregation: 2,800 burst token-equivalents during 15-minute window, classified as burst because dedicated reserve utilization surpassed 92% temporarily due to blended queued requests from partner proxy and customer traffic.

Correlated GitHub deploys: partner infra had a redeploy (streamset/proxy-service@commit:4f9d3a) at 2026-03-08 01:59 UTC that re-enabled legacy header rewrite. See PR https://github.com/streamset/proxy-service/pull/487
Tested reenactment in a sandbox: simulated proxy rewrite produced identical request attribution pattern and triggered burst-charge classification in the billing pipeline.
resolution_notes: Applied provisional credit of $1,120 to BlueHarbor Analytics invoice INV-2026-03-08-BH-0042 on 2026-03-13. Credit applied to pending autopay to allow payment to proceed.

Removed all postback attributions mapping to aws-int-77 in billing reconciler and backfilled corrected attributions for the 02:11–02:26 UTC window; confirmed that corrected attribution removes duplicate counting.

Coordinated with partner 'StreamSet Partners' to remove legacy header rewrite and pushed an outbound advisory recommending a safe-delete window for decommissioned integrations. Partner PR identified and rolled back at 2026-03-09 04:20 UTC.

Created follow-up internal task INT-722: add an automated inventory drift detection rule to Cloud Integrations to detect orphaned mapping and self-validate after partner deploys. Assigned to Cloud Integrations team; target ETA 2026-04-10.
Customer communication: final RCA and steps provided via email and ticket; customer acknowledged and closed dispute after credit.
